decision: Escalate to the property manager for compliance ownership. The annual gas check was carried out on 9 October 2025 but Flintmere has not issued the signed Landlord Gas Safety Record and has given no date; the last signed record on file is dated 16 October 2024, so the CLK-GAS-CP12 12-month renewal point passed on 16 October 2025 with the tenant in occupation. The playbook requires an expired or missing certificate with a tenant in occupation to be escalated so a human owns the statutory follow-up. Within authority I chased Flintmere in writing for the signed record, an issue date, the appliance list and a quote for the lockout diagnostic (ACT-1); told the tenant the portal screenshot is not her gas safety record and gave gas-emergency and heating-failure advice (ACT-2); gave the landlord the outstanding list she asked for on 17 October (ACT-3); and logged the finding (ACT-4). I did not dispatch a diagnostic: the boiler restarts on reset, heating is working and no gas smell is reported, so it is not an emergency; there is no standing spend cap on file and the landlord has twice refused spend without her written agreement (APR-SPEND-OVER-CAP, event-016, event-023). I did not issue gas-portal-record.pdf to the tenant as her certificate — it is a job-card screenshot marked "Customer document: Processing", and telling a tenant the property is certified while sources disagree is prohibited by the playbook.
